subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Revenue Recognition Fraud
description: A micro-lesson that makes Revenue Recognition Fraud usable.

hook.text: A company books revenue from a deal that hasn't closed yet. Sales look amazing. The deal falls through.

buildup.text: Revenue recognition fraud records sales too early, inflates figures, or fabricates transactions entirely.

discovery.text: It's the most common form of financial statement fraud, appearing in over 50% of SEC enforcement cases.

twist.text: Channel stuffing — forcing extra products on distributors — technically books real revenue, but it's misleading.

climax.text: Revenue fraud is tempting because Wall Street rewards growth. Miss the target and the stock tanks.

punchline.text: Book it now. Ship it later. Hope nobody checks.

quiz.question: What is revenue recognition fraud?
options: Recording sales too early or fabricating transactions
Failing to collect payments from customers
Reporting revenue in the wrong currency
